# Master work plan — audit remediation, 2026-08-03

> **Status:** ACTIVE — created 2026-08-03 and updated through 2026-08-21. This is the
> authoritative status tracker for open work. It supersedes `WORK_PLAN_2026-07-17.md`
> as the top-level tracker.
>
> **Scope:** every actionable architecture, security, feature, package/build, design,
> accessibility, privacy, documentation, and release finding from the 2026-08-03 Codex audit and its
> subsequent skeptical rechecks. Older plans remain useful implementation research; the primary-task register below records
> every current id, while §17 preserves the older-id reconciliation.

The audit found a strong foundation, not a rewrite candidate. This plan therefore keeps the
offline-first architecture, encrypted database, centralized event and authentication boundaries,
durable outgoing queue, and existing product direction. The work is about making the current design
safer, easier to maintain, and honestly release-ready.

No implementation item in this file was complete merely because the plan was written. Check an item
only after its acceptance criteria and verification steps pass.

---

## 1. How to use this plan

- Use the stable item id in branch names, commits, tests, and device-checklist entries.
- Treat batch order as dependency order, not as a wall between unrelated work. A device-, server-, or
  owner-blocked tail may stay open while the next independent host-verifiable P0/P1 slice proceeds; record that
  transition in the register and evidence ledger.
- Split every `L` item into reviewed sub-PRs; never land a large cross-cutting rewrite in one pass.
- Preserve unrelated user changes and re-read the complete diff before closing an item.
- If device behavior contradicts a Node/Jest test, stop and treat the device result as the new fact.
- A code item is not done until its focused tests and the common gate in §14 pass.
- A native item is not done until the exact candidate build passes its device checks.
- Update status only here. Companion documents may hold design detail, but must link back to this file.

Tracking syntax:

- The heading checkbox is completion only: `[ ]` open, `[x]` done.
- Every primary heading appears exactly once in the status register below as `TODO`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `DONE`,
  `BLOCKED`, `WAIVED`, or `DROPPED`. `BLOCKED` names the exact external input in §16; `WAIVED` must satisfy §16;
  `DROPPED` needs an owner decision.
- When work starts, add/update a detailed evidence-ledger row with owner, branch/PR, last-updated date, and evidence.
  Child slices and verification checkpoints may appear there without changing the primary-task count. Remove no
  historical evidence row; mark it done and keep the link.

Priority:

- **P0:** release blocker or confirmed privacy/correctness defect.
- **P1:** complete before substantial new feature work.
- **P2:** planned hardening or product improvement.
- **P3:** later breadth or decision-gated work.

Size:

- **S:** one focused change.
- **M:** several modules or one native surface.
- **L:** must be split into independently verified slices.

An `L` parent is an epic, not an executable PR. If child ids/criteria are not already listed, its first permitted
action is a small design/decomposition update to this plan; implementation cannot start under the parent id alone.

Markers:

- **DEVICE:** requires physical/emulated Android verification.
- **CROSS-REPO:** requires a compatible server/helper change.
- **DECISION:** needs an explicit product/owner choice before the final implementation step.

Release disposition is independent of engineering priority:

- **BLOCKER:** the exact candidate cannot ship while the item is open.
- **CONDITIONAL:** the item may remain open only when the affected feature and claim are disabled in the exact
  candidate, with proof that the vulnerable path is unreachable.
- **NONBLOCKING:** may follow the release after its residual risk is documented.

An item omitted from §3.1 is **BATCH-REQUIRED** by default: it must close for its assigned batch or be explicitly
rescheduled in the execution ledger, but it is not a public-release blocker merely because it is in this plan.
This default prevents an unlisted task from having undefined exit semantics; it never overrides a listed
BLOCKER/CONDITIONAL disposition or the final candidate gate.

A lower-priority task can still be a release blocker, and a high-priority build cleanup can be nonblocking if its
risk is proven unreachable. §3.1 is authoritative for release disposition.

## 4. Non-regression guardrails

The audit also identified choices that are already good. Preserve them while implementing this plan.

- [x] **`GUARD-01` — Core stays platform-free.** `src/core` must not import React, React Native,
      Expo, Zustand, UI, or the native DB. `REL-011A` now enforces this with five mutation/parser tests and a live
      scan of all 65 core files; the larger `REL-011` parent remains open.
- [ ] **`GUARD-02` — DB stays the UI source of truth.** Network, socket, FCM, and outgoing
      reconciliation write durable state before UI/notification side effects.
- [ ] **`GUARD-03` — One event ingress.** New socket and push events continue through `EventRouter`;
      failed processing remains retryable and source/dedup behavior is tested.
- [ ] **`GUARD-04` — One authentication boundary.** Passwords stay out of URLs by default and are
      added by `HttpClient`; no feature builds its own authenticated transport casually.
- [ ] **`GUARD-05` — Encryption is not weakened.** SQLCipher, SecureStore, crash-safe rekey, and the
      authenticated backup format remain covered during DB/package changes.
- [ ] **`GUARD-06` — Durable sending remains idempotent.** New scheduling, cancellation, or UI work
      must use the existing queue leases and original temporary identifiers.
- [ ] **`GUARD-07` — Capability gates remain authoritative.** Unsupported server features stay hidden
      or show an explicit fallback; client UI never assumes a server route exists.
- [ ] **`GUARD-08` — Headless registration remains at the bundle entry.** FCM, notify-kit, and
      background-task registration stay imported by `index.js` before `expo-router/entry`.
- [ ] **`GUARD-09` — Reactive-set replacements stay add-then-prune.** Contacts, participants, groups,
      and similar sets may never expose a transient empty state.
- [ ] **`GUARD-10` — Tombstone predicates stay identical.** Chat visibility, unread flooring, preview,
      un-hide writes, search, filters, recovery, and pagination must share the existing deletion rules.
- [x] **`GUARD-11` — Migration ids are allocated at merge time.** Planned work never reserves distant
      migration numbers; every schema PR receives the next visible id during merge preparation and records it.
      `MIG-01` enforces the registry with five tests across the current 38 sequential migrations.

| Guard                              | Enforcement owner                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GUARD-01`                         | `REL-011A` restricted imports                                            |
| `GUARD-02`, `GUARD-09`, `GUARD-10` | `DB-02A..C`, `PERF-02`, `RECOVERY-02` invariant/architecture tests       |
| `GUARD-03`                         | `PUSH-RETRY-01`, `REL-008` EventRouter/idempotency tests                 |
| `GUARD-04`                         | `REL-006`, `RT-01A`, `REL-011D` transport/import rules                   |
| `GUARD-05`                         | `DB-01`, `DB-03`, `FILE-01A..B`, backup tests                            |
| `GUARD-06`                         | `PUSH-RETRY-01`, `SCHED-01`, existing outgoing-queue contract tests      |
| `GUARD-07`                         | `FEAT-03..07` capability/fallback tests                                  |
| `GUARD-08`                         | `BUILD-01`, `REL-011D`, `DEVICE-01` entry/autolink/killed-process checks |
| `GUARD-11`                         | `MIG-01` merge-time registry/check                                       |

The relevant guard is checked as part of each item; the boxes above close when automated enforcement
exists, not merely because the rule is documented.

“Main items” means assigned to the batch, not that every decision-gated enhancement blocks its exit. A batch exits
when all assigned **BLOCKER** items are done, every assigned **CONDITIONAL** item is either done or disabled with
candidate proof, every **BATCH-REQUIRED** item is done or explicitly rescheduled, and any unfinished
**NONBLOCKING** item has a destination batch/status in the execution ledger.
Thus `RT-01B`, strict `LOCK-01B`, and other cross-repo/advanced branches do not freeze their batch after the safe
containment branch has closed.

Public release follows §3.1 disposition, not priority alone: every BLOCKER closes and every CONDITIONAL path is
fixed or disabled with exact-candidate proof. Large nonblocking DB/documentation work may continue after an
internal build, but no broad feature batch starts before Batches 0–8 close or receive an allowed, documented
disposition under §16.

## 7. Workstream B — network and WebView trust boundaries

### [ ] `NET-01` — Build a bounded, private-network-safe preview pipeline

- **Priority/size:** P1 / L; **CONDITIONAL** while `NET-00` keeps in-app preview fetching disabled. Depends on
  `DEC-01`.
- **Child slices:** `NET-01A` transport/proxy decision and threat model; `NET-01B` canonical URL/DNS/address/
  redirect policy; `NET-01C` bounded HTML and image streaming; `NET-01D` Android adversarial proof. The epic is
  not ready to start as one PR.
- **Scope:** Validate literal and DNS-resolved IPv4/IPv6 addresses, prevent DNS rebinding/address changes,
  inspect every redirect before it is requested, apply the same rules to preview images, cap decompressed
  bytes while streaming, enforce timeouts/content types, and never attach Gator authentication.
- **Acceptance:** Public URLs work only after user action. Zero socket/HTTP request reaches a private/reserved
  address from the initial URL, any DNS answer, redirect, or preview image. The transport connects to the exact
  validated address without validate-then-re-resolve time-of-check/time-of-use exposure; decompressed bytes are
  capped before whole-body allocation, canceled responses leave no partial state, and RN auto-follow fetch is not
  treated as sufficient.
- **Verify:** Pure URL/address table tests; hostile local test servers; Android tests for public-to-private
  redirects and gzip/chunked limits; packet/log proof that protected hosts received no request.

### [ ] `WEB-01` — Remove Find My script/HTML injection

- **Priority/size:** P0 / S.
- **Scope:** Escape `<` when serializing data into HTML and construct marker/popup labels with DOM
  `textContent`, never an HTML string.
- **Acceptance:** Names cannot close the script element or create executable markup in the generated HTML as
  executed by a real WebView, not only in an escaping helper.
- **Verify:** Tests containing `</script>`, event handlers, quotes, ampersands, emoji, and Unicode line
  separators; device map still renders and focuses markers.

### [ ] `WEB-02` — Remove remote executable map code and constrain navigation

- **Priority/size:** P0 / M. Depends on `WEB-01`.
- **Scope:** Bundle a reviewed Leaflet JS/CSS asset, record its version/hash/license, apply a restrictive
  CSP, limit `originWhitelist`, deny file/content access, mixed content, popups/new windows, remote executable
  subframes, and arbitrary top-level navigation; allow only enumerated tile-image hosts and expose no unnecessary
  bridge.
- **Acceptance:** Exact coordinates are never exposed to remotely downloaded executable JavaScript and
  unapproved navigation is blocked before load. Only bundled JavaScript executes.
- **Verify:** Airplane/cache test, real-WebView hostile top-level/subframe/popup/file/content/mixed-content tests,
  and network capture showing no `unpkg` or unapproved script request.

### [ ] `WEB-03` — Restore map attribution and document tile privacy

- **Priority/size:** P0 / S. Depends on `WEB-02`.
- **Scope:** Show visible OpenStreetMap contributor attribution and document that the tile provider sees
  the device IP and requested map region. Send stable app-identifying request headers where the WebView/tile stack
  permits, honor response caching (or cache at least seven days when headers are absent), never bulk-download/
  prefetch, and design for the public tile service's no-SLA/blocking risk—or choose a managed provider. Redacted
  mode must instantiate no map/tile request.
- **Acceptance:** Attribution, headers/cache/rate behavior, fallback, and privacy/store text satisfy the selected
  provider policy.
- **Verify:** Screenshot/generated-HTML tests plus proxy inspection of headers, cache/repeat loads, rate behavior,
  outage fallback, and normal-vs-redacted traffic.

### [ ] `FACE-01` — Apply the WebView policy to FaceTime

- **Priority/size:** P0 / M; **CONDITIONAL**. Reuse `WEB-02` primitives.
- **Scope:** Enumerate exact required Apple HTTPS origins without a broad wildcard; block or externally open all
  other navigation; compare the requesting origin before every camera/microphone grant; deny popups/new windows.
- **Acceptance:** Calling works without granting an attacker-controlled origin access to media.
- **Verify:** Navigation-policy tests and device tests starting with camera/mic already granted, then attempting
  hostile redirects, links, popups, and media requests; both navigation and media grant must be denied.

**Current conditional containment (2026-08-04):** The embedded Find My and FaceTime WebView paths are disabled;
public destinations use the safe system external-browser handoff. `WEB-01..03` and `FACE-01` remain open for any
future re-enable, and the exact candidate still needs native proof that no embedded path is reachable.

### [ ] `RT-01A` — Contain `new-server` rotation on the client

- **Priority/size:** P0 / M; **BLOCKER**.
- **Scope:** Share setup's canonical origin validator; accept HTTPS origins only by default; reject
  credentials, path/query/fragment tricks, downgrades, and silent foreign-host changes. No candidate URL may be
  requested, persisted, or receive credentials before normalized-origin validation and foreground approval.
  Foreign-host approval requires credential reconfirmation; cleartext approval covers REST, socket, upload,
  download, retry, and rotation paths. This item owns validation/persistence; `REL-008` only awaits its effect.
- **Acceptance:** A rejected event causes no network request or persistence. Approved reconnect/persistence is
  awaited and session-epoch protected.
- **Verify:** Parser table, foreign-host/downgrade tests, deferred-session tests, and an integration test
  proving no request or Authorization header reaches a rejected host.

**Current status (2026-08-24): CODE + HOST PROOF COMPLETE / DEVICE PROOF OPEN.** This post-v56 change keeps every
`new-server` instruction ephemeral and outside SQLite. Malformed, credential-bearing, overlong, and HTTPS-to-HTTP
instructions fail closed; an unapproved foreign-host instruction causes no candidate contact. An eligible live
proposal can appear only while the same account is foregrounded, unlocked, connected, and on the expected origin;
approval requires a freshly entered password, plus separate cleartext consent when applicable. Candidate validation
happens before the exclusive, epoch-guarded vault commit and socket replacement. The existing socket can retry only
its already-approved origin.

Focused Node tests pass **9 suites / 174 tests** and focused component tests pass **4 suites / 21 tests**. Independent
security review found and then verified fixes for an overlapping-persistence race and empty-userinfo URL forms. The
full adversarial DB-write scanner passes **94/94**, the inventory reports **1,301 approved mutations** with exact

## 9. Workstream D — cold/headless and realtime reliability

### [ ] `REL-001` — Build a real headless session bootstrap

- **Priority/size:** P0 / M.
- **Scope:** A fresh process reads credentials from the secure vault, applies configured network policy,
  opens the encrypted DB, and constructs sync/outgoing/error services without React or pre-hydrated Zustand.
  Extract a callable pure-orchestrator task body so result behavior is deterministic without waiting for WorkManager.
- **Acceptance:** Vault without credentials is an intentional successful no-op; valid credentials plus completed
  work returns success; transient bootstrap/work failure returns a retryable failure; no decision reads default
  Zustand credentials.
- **Verify:** Unit tests for all result cases from true store defaults; separately trigger a real scheduled/killed-
  process Android wake after `adb shell am kill` and prove a marker/queue changes. Never use force-stop.
- **Current status (2026-08-04):** **IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE / DEVICE PROOF OPEN.** The callable orchestrator
  reads durable session/address/password/app-lock and filesystem revocation state before DB open, constructs one
  task-local client, never reads default Zustand credentials, classifies successful no-op vs retryable failure,
  and stops account-A work after revocation. Production caps each wake at 4 sync pages, 10 schedules, and 10
  outgoing rows. Each headless attachment retry now gets one shared 60-second JavaScript deadline spanning the
  attachment-row lookup, queue file stat, uploader preflight, FIFO gate wait, native transfer, and HTTP response;
  timeout requests native cancellation and records the ordinary retryable queue failure/backoff. This is not a
  whole-wake deadline: claim/outcome commits sit outside it, ten attachment rows can approach ten minutes before
  sync/schedule/diagnostic overhead, and native work can outlive the JavaScript result if Android ignores
  cancellation. Keep this unchecked until a real `adb shell am kill` WorkManager wake changes durable state and
  Failed/offline retry, native cancellation, and timing behavior are observed on Android.

## 11. Workstream F — diagnostics, privacy, policy, and release truthfulness

### [ ] `LOG-01` — Replace blacklist logging with privacy-safe structured diagnostics

- **Priority/size:** P0 / M.
- **Child slices:** `LOG-01A` strict ERROR projection; `LOG-01B` release non-error persistence/export containment;
  `LOG-01C` React Native renderer, persistent-file, and diagnostic-guard hardening; `LOG-01D` remaining opaque
  crash-site token, selected finite schemas, committed app/server fixture, native/pre-runtime containment,
  cleanup-issue retirement, scanner precision, and exact-candidate proof. These names are stable status-log ids, not
  separate primary headings.
- **Scope:** Allowlist metadata; tokenize identifiers with a keyed per-install/per-report HMAC or short-lived opaque
  token rather than plain enumerable hashing; reject untrusted free-form error/response strings before every sink;
  cover camel/snake/nested GUID, handle, address, URL/URI, body/text, and response variants; remove historical
  plaintext logs on upgrade and account logs on disconnect; keep a CI raw-console guard.
- **Acceptance:** Logs remain useful without recoverable message, contact, server, file, or account data.
- **Verify:** Redactor fuzz/table and known-phone enumeration tests; inspect migrated/current file logs, shared
  diagnostics, and uploaded envelopes; prove redaction happens before persistence/export/upload.
- **Current status (2026-08-08):** **IN_PROGRESS — STRICT ERROR, RUNTIME-READY RN, PERSISTENT-FILE, AND SOURCE-GUARD
  CONTAINMENT HOST-GREEN; PRE-RUNTIME/NATIVE AND CANDIDATE PROOF OPEN.** All 20 production ERROR calls use 19 finite
  literal events. Before console/memory/file/DB/HTTP, arbitrary prose and raw stacks are discarded; only allowlisted
  typed fields survive, with a synthetic event-owned frame. `warn`/`info`/`debug` require an explicit development
  runtime and are dropped before message/metadata traversal at the logger/tee boundary and again at built-in sinks.
  The first `index.js` side effect now rebuilds React Native 0.86 renderer exception payloads immediately before the
  native bridge and wraps release console output before any app/headless registration. Caught, uncaught, and
  recoverable errors after the JS runtime is ready therefore retain fatal/nonfatal behavior without forwarding the raw
  Error, component stack, frame paths, cause data, or extra data. This does **not** cover bundle-evaluation/pre-runtime
  failures handled by React Native's C++ path; that explicit residual still needs a native containment decision and
  release-device canary before this item can close.

  Persistent ERROR logging attaches synchronously as the second entry side effect, before the three headless owners.
  Upgrade restore uses `File.info()` rather than the permission-ambiguous `File.exists` and rejects when an unsafe
  legacy plaintext file cannot be inspected/replaced/confirmed deleted. A generation fence deactivates late asynchronous
  continuations, and asynchronous import/read promises have a five-second timeout so a hung promise cannot permanently
  wedge later Clear/flush attempts; Expo's synchronous `info`/`write`/`delete` calls cannot be interrupted by a JavaScript
  timer and therefore are not claimed as time-bounded. Failed flushes stay dirty and retry. Background sync, FCM, and
  notify-kit headless callbacks now await a finite three-attempt best-effort persistence barrier before settling, including
  an already in-flight disk operation; exact killed-process durability remains a device-proof item rather than a host-only
  guarantee. App Logs keeps its visible snapshot until deletion is confirmed, disables overlapping Clear/Share operations,
  and reports share-sheet failure. A foreground cleanup failure emits a degraded six-second toast that points to App Logs,
  where an accessible persistent warning keeps the Clear-and-restart remediation visible. After native deletion is
  confirmed, that warning changes to an explicit restart-verification state that survives route remounts. Its filters and
  actions use separate wrapping rows so Clear remains reachable on narrow screens and with larger text. Successful manual
  Clear still does not retire the process-cached initialization issue until restart; same-process issue retirement and
  exact-device proof remain open.

  The source guard now has 30 mutation tests. It rejects dynamic/unknown ERROR messages, logger/sink/global-console
  aliases, object/return/re-export and call/apply/bind/sequence forwarding, changes to either tightly owned console
  boundary, direct known-sink writes, and dynamic/unknown native output. Its Kotlin/Java scan covers executable string
  templates, aliases/callable references/star imports, and every generated `android/app/src` source set; CI reruns it
  after clean prebuild. All six approved native calls now use the fully qualified `android.util.Log.w` receiver, exact
  literal `"GatorPasteInput"` tag, and one finite literal message; native imports and shadowable `Log` receivers are
  rejected. Java preprocessing implements the JLS 3.3 eligible-backslash rule and JLS 3.8 identifier-ignorable
  normalization, including raw/escaped format and control characters before lexical filtering. The complete owned
  Kotlin file is hash-pinned and must be scanned exactly once at its exact root-relative path; missing, duplicated,
  suffix-decoy, or symlink-hidden owner paths fail closed.
  Fuzz/enumeration/hostile-object tests cover the strict runtime path. Migration
  `0034_purge_legacy_error_reports` deletes every pre-policy queued diagnostic row on upgrade because old raw rows cannot
  be distinguished safely from strict rows by shape; current projected rows can be inserted normally afterward. A
  privacy-safe opaque crash-site token, a committed app↔server contract fixture, selected high-value finite non-error
  schemas, same-process cleanup-issue retirement, pre-runtime/native containment, and exact-candidate
  file/share/logcat/HTTP inspection remain open. Do not close `LOG-01` on host automation alone.

## 12. Workstream G — database ownership and real-driver safety

### [ ] `DB-01` — Own the Drizzle/op-sqlite compatibility boundary

- **Priority/size:** P1 / M. `PKG-01` owns exact pins; `REL-009A` owns failed-open cleanup.
- **Scope:** Own the explicit adapter contract, upgrade playbook, and tests for row shapes, raw execution,
  builders, `RETURNING`, writes, rollback, and reactive flush against both Node and actual Android.
- **Acceptance:** A dependency change cannot silently invalidate the Proxy adapter.
- **Verify:** Controlled incompatible fake/version test and Android SQLCipher contract suite.
- **Current status (2026-08-21):** **IN_PROGRESS — LOCAL API-35 DRIVER, REPOSITORY-HEAD MIGRATION, CONTROLLED
  RELAUNCH, ORDINARY ACTIVE-WAL WRITE-DEATH, AND POST-STATEMENT ACTIVE-MIGRATION DEATH CONTRACTS GREEN;
  POWER/CI/RELEASE HARDWARE OPEN.** Child
  `DB-01A-SYNC-EXECUTE-REACTIVE-FLUSH` makes every installed Drizzle write
  route request a reactive-query flush. Child `DB-01B-ANDROID-DRIVER-CONTRACT` exercises the actual
  SQLCipher/op-sqlite/Drizzle stack on an API-35 arm64 emulator: encrypted open, wrong-key rejection, FTS5,
  commit/rollback reactive convergence, all three adapter routes, rekey, key-specific reopen, and cleanup pass against
  a disposable database. Child
  `DB-03A-ANDROID-MIGRATION-CONTRACT` runs the exact production migration runner from `0001` through `0038`, proves
  per-migration `0030` rollback/retry over an audited head-`0029` fixture, and validates the production FTS triggers,
  migration ledger/data, integrity, and idempotency on that same disposable file. Child
  `DB-03B1-ANDROID-PROCESS-RELAUNCH` uses a separate fixed disposable file: process A emits READY while retaining its
  encrypted handle; the harness force-stops A, observes no process, then requires a distinct process B to verify the
  preserved head-`0029` state read-only before any write and apply exact `0030`–`0038`. Child
  `DB-03B2A-REPOSITORY-HEAD-MATRIX` adds same-process encrypted logical fixtures for the reviewed repository heads
  `0024` and `0027`, while retaining the existing `0029` path. Child
  `DB-03B2B1-ACTIVE-WAL-WRITE-DEATH` reuses the exclusive DEV dispatcher with a third fixed disposable file: process A
  commits a WAL baseline, checkpoints it, then stays alive with a bounded ordinary write transaction open; after the
  host observes physical WAL growth and crashes that exact process, distinct process B first proves the exact baseline
  read-only with every uncommitted row absent, then commits and reopens a recovery row and cleans the fixed state.
  `DB-03B2B2-ACTIVE-MIGRATION-DEATH` uses a fourth fixed disposable file and the exact production migration runner:
  process A reaches exact head `0037`, commits an exact 133-row fixture, and pauses only after migration `0038`'s
  `UPDATE` has resolved inside its still-open transaction while the ledger remains at `0037`; after the host crashes A,
  distinct process B first proves the exact head-`0037` pre-migration state read-only, then retries exact `0038` and
  verifies persistence and cleanup. This does not prove a statement-in-flight crash. Power-loss/torn-write recovery,
  actual historical signed/store artifacts, spontaneous OS death, scheduled CI, the production database, and exact
  release-candidate/physical hardware remain open.

### [x] `DB-02A` — Inventory and gate every runtime write

- **Priority/size:** P0 / M; release-blocking fact-finding and containment.
- **Scope:** Regenerate the write inventory, classify transaction ownership, locate ordinary writes that can
  join unrelated transactions, and stress the documented nested/bystander hazards. Add a temporary CI allowlist so
  every mutation has an approved owner and one of two release-safe dispositions: it uses the serialized coordinator,
  or a focused test proves that no runtime transaction can temporally overlap it.
- **Acceptance:** Every write path has one named owner and a proven disposition; new unapproved raw writes fail CI;
  each reachable or unproven hazard has a focused containment task. A named owner alone is not sufficient, and the
  release allowlist contains no ordinary writer whose non-overlap is merely assumed. If evidence disproves the need
  for a global rewrite, preserve only the exceptions with enforceable temporal-exclusion proof.
- **Verify:** Mutation-check the guard by adding forbidden writes in repositories, services, UI, sync, and native
  support paths.
- **Current status (2026-08-21):** **DONE — EXACT FAIL-CLOSED INVENTORY COMPLETE; ALL 1,300 CURRENT FINDINGS PROVED.**
  `scripts/check-db-writes.mjs` combines a direct TypeScript-AST SQL/Drizzle scan with a
  whole-runtime TypeScript symbol graph. It follows immutable aliases, barrel re-exports, local callbacks,
  transitive wrappers, `.call`/`.apply`, static namespace access, and transaction callback positions. Writer
  references, mutable/bound/destructured escapes, computed namespace dispatch, unresolved coordinator callbacks,
  and potential nested coordinator entry fail closed. Anonymous callbacks use declaration identity and stable
  lexical fingerprints rather than names or line numbers. Owned native source is separately rejected on SQLite/
  Room markers.

  **Faster proof workflow (2026-08-13):** `test/support/dbOwnershipProof.ts` now supplies the reusable
  rolling-neighbour controller and observable-promise helper for ownership tests. A test should await the
  neighbour's `entered` gate, retain and assert the owner/successor promises, call `cleanup()` in `finally`, drain
  every observed successor, and only then close the database. This replaces the repeated hand-built deferred/
  rollback cleanup that made each earlier ownership slice slow and error-prone.

  `npm run reconcile:db-writes` is the safe default and never writes. Run it once before DB-source work to establish
  a clean **0 line shifts / 0 rekeys / 0 additions** baseline, then rerun it after the bounded source edit. Review
  every proposed change. The reconciler may refresh a same-ID line, preserve reviewed metadata across one unique
  callback-fingerprint rekey only when the unchanged write snippet reconstructs both IDs, or add a genuinely new
  record as explicitly `unproven`. Stale removals, changed scanner/context fields, changed write snippets, duplicate
  IDs, and ambiguous cardinality fail closed. Use `npm run reconcile:db-writes -- --write` only after that output
  matches the reviewed source change; it atomically applies only the mechanical reconciliation, never ownership
  approval or evidence. The 2026-08-13 live dry run was already **0 / 0 / 0**, so `--write` was not run and inventory
  SHA-256 `41043f39b5519aed6fbf9bc80ee6f250fe7af286378d3f6a6eb54d6029219e2c` remained byte-identical.

  The initial exact inventory on 2026-08-12 contained **1,072 entries**: 271 direct mutation sites, 779 resolved
  mutator calls, 19 mutator-reference escapes, and 3 unresolved coordinator callbacks. At that checkpoint, membership
  was exact with **0 structural, nested-coordinator, or membership errors**; 94 startup migration/initialization sites
  had proved temporal exclusion, 487 writes/calls were scanner-recognized coordinated paths, and the other **491
  entries remained explicitly `unproven`** with no invented approval. The approval gate therefore remained
  intentionally red until the later child milestones below closed those records.

  The 35 scanner tests cover repository/service/UI/native mutations, CTE and `RETURNING` writes, aliases and
  re-exports, transitive calls, same-named callbacks, named transaction callbacks that also escape or run directly,
  dynamic callback forwarding, nested coordinator entry, call/apply/bind/destructuring/computed dispatch, exact
  membership, stale entries, and false positives such as Map/file/HTTP/regex/concurrency APIs. Its one-layer custom
  wrapper inference is closed-world: only stable free functions or direct `const` function bindings qualify; the
  inline coordinator callback must be anonymous and non-generator; every forwarded callback lifetime must be
  directly awaited or returned; a plain returned task is rejected when an enclosing `finally` can replace it, while
  `return await` remains provable. Mutable aliases, `arguments`, method/property wrappers, self-escape, namespace
  dispatch, spread arguments, or any unresolved reference reject inference. The production
  `withCurrentDeliveryTransaction` wrapper satisfies that contract, so all 5 opener calls and 14 callback/callee
  edges are now recognized without a prose-only approval.

  Server-error reconciliation also no longer has an optional dual ownership mode: the public APIs always own one
  short transaction, while the realtime sink calls explicit transaction-only bodies inside its existing guarded
  delivery transaction. Retry-cycle state is returned as an idempotent post-commit effect, so a durable checkpoint,
  account guard, or SQL COMMIT failure rolls back the queue without spending the in-memory cycle cap. Those 19
  realtime findings plus 6 public-wrapper findings are the only newly approved entries in this slice. Next work is
  to classify callers and fix one reachable uncoordinated writer at a time; `DB-02A` cannot close, and the approval
  check cannot enter CI, until no ordinary path remains unproven.

  Error-report upload outcomes now have the same unambiguous ownership: `claimErrorReports`,
  `markErrorReportsFailed`, and `deleteErrorReports` always queue one bounded transaction whether or not the caller
  supplies an account commit guard. Their production batch is capped at 100 IDs, safely below SQLite's bind limit;
  the exported boundary deduplicates IDs and rejects more than 100 unique IDs before any write. Duplicate failure
  IDs count once and missing rows are harmless. Rolling-neighbour tests prove the unguarded forms cannot silently
  join another transaction and disappear with its rollback. Six public-wrapper findings are newly proved by this
  slice.

  `retireOutgoing` is no longer the last optional-guard dual-mode writer: its guard now authorizes commit while the
  public helper always owns one two-statement transaction. A rolling-neighbour regression proves an unguarded
  retirement waits instead of joining a rollback, and a forced second-statement failure proves the retry cap rolls
  back with the bubble update. Four retire findings are newly proved. Formal one-row/lookup boundedness remains a
  separate schema follow-up because `outgoing_queue.temp_guid` is not indexed or uniquely constrained; that migration
  decision is deliberately not hidden inside this ownership slice.

  transaction-neutral `claimOutgoing` / `markOutgoingSending` halves and the service's outer transaction. Its lease

  the optional account guard authorizes that commit without changing ownership. A skeptical review caught that the
  first version captured the lease timestamp before waiting for the global mutex, which could commit an already-
  expired lease after a long wait. The helper now accepts a clock callback and reads it only after lock acquisition.
  Rolling-neighbour, second-write rollback, and queued-clock regressions prove isolation, atomicity, and a fresh
  lease. Four repository findings are newly proved; the scanner-unresolved service call edge remains honestly
  unproven.

  neither path nests the global mutex. Rolling-neighbour tests prove public batch, single, trim, and clear operations

  generation still rolls back before commit. Eleven findings are newly proved. The explicit transaction-only bodies,

  `DB-02A-DELETE-CHAT-IDENTITY` is **DONE**. `deleteChatLocal` previously resolved a chat GUID to its numeric id
  before entering the process-wide write owner. Because all work shares one SQLite connection, that read could see a
  neighbouring transaction's uncommitted chat. If the neighbour rolled back, SQLite rolled back its AUTOINCREMENT
  sequence too; a queued insert could reuse the same id for an unrelated chat before `deleteChatLocal` began. The
  stale id then tombstoned and purged the innocent replacement while the GUID-keyed queue, schedule, and draft
  deletes targeted the vanished original. This was a reachable data-loss defect, not scanner-only hardening.

  The one-production-file fix moves GUID lookup inside `deleteChatLocal`'s owning transaction, fences its UPDATE by
  both id and GUID, and returns the exact committed `{chatId, boundary}` pair for the separate purge. Missing or
  changed identity now returns a no-op before any decision delete or purge. `src/db/repositories/chats.ts` changed
  from SHA-256 `f1afe5d9f95f6a4fc605945ec677361a4b8ca5e1f6589f047a70ea77853fcf08` to

  change: `runTrackedRealtimeWork` already admits and drains exact-account work before wipe/reconnect. The
  500-message purge chunks intentionally remain separate post-commit owners; their total count and duration are not
  claimed to be globally bounded.

  terms from FTS after the search backfill marker was already complete. Overlapping edits could additionally strand a

  is UI-gated because Edit requires a truthy selected text; the production-reachable defects were the pre-lock
  dirty/stale snapshot and overlapping same-message lifecycles, while the fallback closes the adjacent recovery gap.

  `applyLocalEdit` now snapshots committed text, exact attributed body, prior edit marker, and chat identity and applies
  the optimistic text in one short DB-only transaction. It clears `attributed_body` while the optimistic edit is live,
  because message rendering prefers that rich body over `text`. After commit, outside the mutex, empty/null stored text
  uses decoded text from the exact snapshotted body when available and otherwise preserves the original null-versus-empty
  value. Failure restores that effective searchable text, the byte-exact prior body, and the prior marker. The revert
  compare-and-set requires the optimistic marker and text and a still-cleared body, so an authoritative echo with a
  differing text or restored rich body is preserved. Missing rows do not POST, missing chat identity is compensated
  before returning, and unsend behavior is unchanged.

  mutation cannot redirect cleanup, and the same GUID on another account DB proceeds independently. The existing
  `runUiAccountOperation` adoption means Disconnect drains admitted edits before wiping the account.

### [ ] `DB-02B` — Introduce explicit transaction-scoped primitives

- **Priority/size:** P0 / L for confirmed reachable paths. Depends on `DB-02A` evidence.
- **Child slices:** `DB-02B1` writer plus branded transaction API; `DB-02B2` conversion of existing transaction
  owners/high-risk paths.
- **Scope:** One serialized writer/executor owns runtime operations. Application services open a transaction and
  must pass a branded explicit transaction handle to non-transacting primitives. The type/API makes nested entry
  structurally unavailable; do not use a module-global `inTransaction` flag, which misclassifies legitimate
  concurrent Hermes callers.
- **Acceptance:** The API shape prevents an internal-transacting helper from being called inside another
  transaction.
- **Verify:** Compile-time/API tests, prompt nesting failure, and rollback tests proving unrelated writes survive.
- **Current status (2026-08-26):** **IN_PROGRESS — `DB-02B1` and `DB-02B2A`–`DB-02B2AI` DONE; `DB-02B2` remainder OPEN.** The serialized writer,
  opaque branded `DbTransactionContext`, private runtime `WeakMap` authentication, synchronous join registration,
  stale/forged/late-context rejection, and fail-closed direct/transitive nested-coordinator scanner were already
  implemented and verified under `DB-02A-RUNTIME-TRANSACTION-CONTEXT-JOIN`. A compile-only negative contract now
  closes the remaining B1 proof gap: the owner token can call transaction-only helpers, but cannot typecheck as a raw
  database for a standalone self-transacting helper or as the database argument to another `withDbTransaction`; raw
  databases and arbitrary objects cannot typecheck as the token.

### [ ] `DB-02C` — Migrate all writers and stress concurrency

- **Priority/size:** P1 / L. Depends on `DB-02B`; required for every writer that lacks the temporal-exclusion proof
  demanded by `DB-02A`.
- **Child slices:** `DB-02C1` sync/live events; `DB-02C2` sends/retries/schedules; `DB-02C3`
  contacts/settings/downloads; `DB-02C4` exclusive maintenance, wipe/rekey, and removal of the temporary allowlist.
- **Scope:** Move every unproven runtime writer onto the coordinator by subsystem. Define two modes: short DB-only
  bounded runtime operations; and exclusive maintenance for migration/wipe/rekey, which pauses new writes and chunks
  deletion where possible while preserving rekey atomicity. A remaining exception needs an automated proof that no
  runtime transaction can overlap it. Never run unbounded wipe/rekey inside the short mode.
- **Acceptance:** There is no path for a bystander write to join a transaction or for nested work to wedge the
  process-wide queue. The final release allowlist contains no unproven ordinary writer; each exception has an
  executable temporal-exclusion test and a named owner.
- **Verify:** Concurrent sync/live-message/upload/rollback/rekey stress test, watchdog assertions, and device run.

**Workstream exit:** every runtime mutation uses the coordinator or has automated proof that no runtime transaction
can overlap it; nested transaction construction is impossible on coordinated paths; unrelated writes survive
rollback; final persistent account wipe passes; and native-driver contracts run outside Jest. A global migration is
not required merely for architectural uniformity, but an unproven ordinary-writer exception is never release-safe.

- **Priority/size:** P0 / M. Depends on every selected release-blocking item.
- **Scope:** Run common/static/native gates, clean AAB build, merged-manifest inspection, dependency/license notices,
  privacy/Data Safety/listing reconciliation, target SDK 36 requirement for the 2026-08-31 Play deadline (reverify
  current policy), upgrade/install tests, and rollout/support plan. Record any permitted waiver with owner, reason,
  user impact, compensating control, and revisit date.
- **Acceptance:** No unchecked release BLOCKER; every CONDITIONAL feature is fixed or unreachable in the exact
  candidate with evidence. Credential exfiltration, executable injection, media-permission escape, and unbounded
  input cannot be waived without a tested compensating control/disablement and security/privacy approval. Artifact
  hash and evidence are retained.
- **Verify:** §14 plus candidate device matrix and Play pre-launch/policy checks.

## 14. Common verification gates

The gates are cumulative. `BASE-01` is complete, so Gate B is the current code gate; Gate A is retained only to
reproduce the historical baseline. Gate C is implemented and its local release-variant smoke run is green, but
`SDK-01` remains open for clean-install and focused package/device smoke evidence. Gate C never substitutes for the
static/test signal in Gate B. Add the
dependency/native gates below whenever their change class applies, without dropping the cumulative gates.

### Gate A — historical baseline, before `BASE-01`

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npx prettier --check "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}" "app/**/*.{ts,tsx}" "test/**/*.{ts,tsx}"
npm test -- --runInBand
```

The recorded historical baseline had 14 warnings. `BASE-01B` has closed that debt; current runs use Gate B and may
not reintroduce warnings.

### Gate B — clean code signal, after `BASE-01`

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint -- --max-warnings=0
npm run format:check
npm test -- --runInBand
```

### Gate C — Expo compatibility (implemented; native `SDK-01` proof still open)

```sh
CI=1 npx expo install --check
npm run doctor
```

`doctor` uses an exact Expo Doctor version. The current check passes 20/20 and Expo reports dependencies up to date;
never use `@latest` in a reproducible gate.

Dependency/package batches additionally:

```sh
npm ci
npm audit --audit-level=high
npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high
npm ls --depth=0
```

Heavy native/config gates run for package, config, native-module, and candidate-release lanes—not blindly for every
JS-only change. Use a clean generated Android project or disposable worktree:

```sh
npx expo prebuild --platform android --clean
npx expo-modules-autolinking search -p android
cd android
./gradlew \
  :gator-paste-input:testDebugUnitTest \
  :gator-bounded-download:testDebugUnitTest \
  :gator-paste-input:compileDebugKotlin \
  :gator-share-shortcuts:compileDebugKotlin \
  :gator-bounded-download:compileDebugKotlin \
  :app:assembleDebug \
  --no-daemon
./gradlew :app:bundleRelease --no-daemon
cd ..
npm run check:android-build
```

Inspect the merged/release manifest or AAB rather than trusting `app.config.ts` alone. Killed-process push tests
must use `adb shell am kill <package>`; `am force-stop` deliberately prevents broadcast delivery and is not a valid
memory-reclamation test.

For any test added to protect a load-bearing invariant, briefly break the source and confirm the test fails before
restoring it. This prevents a green test that never exercised the intended branch.

## 16. External blockers and waiver rules

The eight primary tasks currently marked **BLOCKED** cannot be completed solely by editing this repository:

- `LEGAL-01`: project owner/legal approval of the license, copyright, and inherited notices.
- `RT-01B`: compatible signed-rotation protocol, key ownership, and rollout from the app and server owners.
- `PUSH-CRYPTO-01`: versioned server key/envelope/replay protocol plus a migration decision.
- `DELETE-SYNC-01`: a lossless server continuation and snapshot-consistent initial-cursor/history contract.
- `PLAY-02`: Play Console full-screen-intent eligibility/declaration access from the release/product owner.
- `PLAY-03`: owner contacts-product decision plus Play declaration/account access.
- `ALIAS-SEND-01`: a server/helper capability and validated per-message sender-alias field.
- `DEVICE-01`: exact Play delivery of local candidate `0.1.41` / version code `57`, a refreshed v57 checklist,
  representative Android hardware/emulators, an isolated staged server/fixture, Firebase, and release credentials.
  The local AAB and its static identity proof exist; none of those external runtime inputs or results does.

Other tasks have useful repository work available and therefore remain `IN_PROGRESS` or `TODO`, but their final
acceptance still depends on named outside evidence or decisions:

- `PRIV-02`: an owner decision whether a legacy stored `1` qualifies as prior informed diagnostic consent; without
  that decision, its existing-install behavior contradicts the stated default-off scope.
- `SUPPORT-01`: real owner-approved privacy, license/notices, and support destinations.
- `SUPPLY-01`, `ENV-01`, `BUILD-01`: required-check, environment-smoke, and exact-candidate device evidence. The owner
  requires release-candidate builds to remain local; hosted EAS builds are not a supported closure path.
- `PUSH-RETRY-01`: server/Firebase/connected-FCM/exact-candidate evidence, including the attempt-id contract.
- `LOG-01`: a committed app/server diagnostic fixture, native/pre-runtime decision, and exact-candidate file/share/
  logcat/network inspection.
- `STORE-01`: the exact v57 candidate exists locally, but exclusive Internal Testing closure still needs an authorized
  Play Console account, live track/tester/link/signing confirmation, separately approved upload/submission, isolated
  staged-server access and fixtures, candidate-notice approval, artifact-specific prompts, Play install/update,
  cleanup, and exact-device results. The feedback route alone is owner-confirmed. `STORE-01A-UGC-SAFETY` remains a
  pre-promotion backlog item rather than a current Internal Testing blocker.
- `DEC-07` / `ANDROID-01`, `ANDROID-03A..B`: Play device-catalog data and an owner support decision.
- `BACKUP-SLOTS-01` and `FEAT-06`: server/helper contracts must be reverified before implementation can close.

`DEVICE-01` supplies a shared candidate environment; it does not automatically close any task-specific device
acceptance criterion. Each owning task must link its own result.

An external blocker does not justify marking the item complete. Mark it **BLOCKED** in this file with the
exact missing input, finish all repository-side preparation/tests, and move only to work that does not hide the
same release risk.

A release waiver must record:

1. item id and exact unverified behavior;
2. user/security impact;
3. mitigation or disabled feature;
4. approving owner;
5. security/privacy approval where applicable;
6. exact candidate proof that a CONDITIONAL path is disabled;
7. expiry/revisit date.

Credential exfiltration, executable injection, media-permission escape, and unbounded input cannot be waived by
risk acceptance alone; they require tested path disablement or a compensating control.

  adopts one inline join. The public `insertOutgoingContact` signature remains compatible for standalone callers.
  Committed chat lookup, contact retry-row insertion, optimistic message insertion, and NULL-safe monotonic chat-date
  advancement now share the service's one short guarded transaction.

  Both direct and post-picker UI front doors pass a guard from their captured account lease; native permission/picker
  work remains outside SQLite and the logical-send queue. The service rechecks that lease after COMMIT and before HTTP,
  passes the same guard into successful and failed settlement, and rethrows guard rejection rather than attempting a
  second stale-account failure owner. Existing temp/real GUID, structured contact, retry, and reply semantics remain
  intact. The supported payload excludes top-level native contact IDs, photo paths, unrelated selected text, and empty
  attachment/reaction arrays.

  The ordinary-send, repository-context, and send-front-door certificates replace six old core records with nine
  explicit helper-body, wrapper, and service-owner records, while rekeying four outcome/front-door records one-for-one.
  Inventory moves from **1,427** to **1,430 findings / 0 structural or membership errors**, a reviewed net increase of
  three. Ninety-three unchanged findings receive scanner-proven line shifts, and exact reconciliation ends at **0 line
  shifts / 0 rekeys / 0 additions**.

  Under pinned Node **24.19.0**, strict TypeScript passes. `test/db/outgoingBranches.test.ts`,
  `test/db/outgoingUserActions.test.ts`, `test/services/sendContactService.test.ts`,
  `test/services/sendAccountScope.test.ts`, `test/services/sendChatIdentity.test.ts`,
  `test/services/sendRetryGuard.test.ts`, and `test/services/logicalSendQueueWiring.test.ts` pass **7 suites / 119 tests
  / 0 snapshots**. A real SQLite trigger proves lease retirement during the final chat update rolls back all
  provisional state, drains the admitted owner, starts no HTTP, and preserves the predecessor date. A fresh lease then
  commits exact provisional state, observes HTTP with no transaction open, and completes real-GUID promotion. All three
  exact certificates pass **3/3**, the fast scanner passes **84/94** with **10 intentional skips / 0 failed**, and
  Prettier plus `git diff --check` pass. Independent concurrency and scanner/inventory reviews are both **GO**.

  The focused test does not separately retire the lease during post-HTTP settlement or the narrow successful-
  COMMIT→pre-HTTP interval; shared settlement tests and explicit guard wiring cover the constituent behavior. Untyped
  runtime callers could still add nested phone/email keys outside the supported contact shape. Native Expo Contacts,
  real `/message/contact`, op-sqlite/SQLCipher timing, process-kill, and physical teardown remain device/staged evidence.
  Parent `DB-02B` remains **IN_PROGRESS** because text/attachment initial persistence, scheduled handoff, and other
  residual owner conversions remain open. Text and scheduled handoff remain deferred during focused-only work because
  their scheduled-recovery checker coupling requires a broader checker update and full gate. This is post-v57 host proof
  and performs no external write or device action.
